The Ultimate Guide to Holiday Happenings on O‘ahu

Here’s the rundown of all the holiday events across the island where you can get festive through the end of the year.
5 hours ago
Andrea Lee, Jasmine Chagnon,

 

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 35:43
Instaread

Let the holiday season commence! Here’s where to go and what to do to get into the holiday spirit this year, whether you’re looking for Christmas lights or searching for Santa himself. Bookmark this roundup since it’ll be updated regularly.

 

Click to the holiday events you want to explore:

  • Festive Lights & Parades
  • Shopping
  • Food & Drinks
  • Entertainment & Events
  • Trains & Trolleys
  • Photo Opportunities
  • Holiday Drives

 

 

Festive Lights & Parades

 

Photo: Courtesy of Royal Hawaiian Center

 

Royal Hawaiian Center Holiday Kick-Off & Tree Lighting Ceremony

Wednesday, Nov. 25, 5 to 7:30 p.m.

Await the arrival of Aloha Santa with live local music, hula performances and holiday characters. Aloha Santa will lead the lighting of the 34-foot holiday tree decked in Hawaiian ornaments. Stick around to take a free professional photo with him!

 

Free, Royal Hawaiian Center Royal Grove, 2201 Kalākaua Ave., Waikīkī, royalhawaiiancenter.com, @royalhwnctr

 

 

Photo: Aaron K. Yoshino

 

Waikīkī Holiday Parade

Friday, Nov. 27, 7 p.m.

This holiday parade honors survivors of the Dec. 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor and members of the U.S. military with Island bands, military members and local officials, dignitaries, entertainers and more. The torch-lit 1.5-mile night parade begins at Fort DeRussy, continues along Kalākaua Avenue and ends at Kapi‘olani Park.

 

Free, Waikīkī, waikikiholidayparade.com

 

 

Hawai‘i Kai Holiday Parade

Saturday, Nov. 28, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.

The parade will start at the corner of Lunalilo Home Road and Hawai‘i Kai Drive (by the HK Skate Park), head down Lunalilo Home Road and end at Koko Marina Center. Stick around for the Christmas Carnival Celebration from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Koko Marina Center courtyard, which will feature carnival games, holiday crafts, balloon art and Santa Claus. Bring a toy donation to receive 10 free tickets to play the carnival games.

 

Free, Koko Marina Center, 7192 Kalaniana‘ole Highway, Hawai‘i Kai, kokomarinacenter.com, @kokomarinacenter

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Honolulu Parks & Recreation

 

Kapolei City Lights & Holiday Parade

Lights: Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026, through Sunday, Jan. 3, 2027

Block Party: Saturday, Nov. 28, 5 to 9 p.m.

Parade: Saturday, Nov. 28, 5:30 p.m.

Join the Leeward O‘ahu community at a festive block party along the streets surrounding Kapolei Hale. Enjoy food trucks, live entertainment, luminous displays of holiday cheer and a holiday parade. The parade will begin outside of Kapolei High School and end at Kama‘aha Ave. The holiday lights will be displayed nightly until 8 p.m. on weekdays and 10 p.m. on Fridays, weekends and holidays.

 

Free, 1000 Ulu‘ōhia St., Kapolei, honolulu.gov, @kapoleisanta 

 

 

Adventist Health Castle Christmas Tree Lighting

Wednesday, Dec. 2, 5 to 8:30 p.m.

Enjoy music and entertainment and see the Christmas tree light up for the season. A free trolley service to and from the Kailua Town Center parking garage starts at 5 p.m.

 

Free, Adventist Health Castle front lawn, 640 Ulukahiki St., Kailua, kailuatownhi.com, @ah_castle

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of City and County of Honolulu

 

Honolulu City Lights

Saturday, Dec. 5, through the end of the month

View Christmas trees decorated in various themes by City and County of Honolulu departments. Shaka Santa, Tūtū Mele and the snowman family will also be there spreading holiday cheer. On Dec. 5, Mayor Rick Blangiardi will light the city’s 50-foot holiday tree as well as the lights strung up around Honolulu Hale and the Civic Center grounds. Get a free photo with Santa on opening night.

 

Free, parking available in the municipal lot at Alapai and Beretania St., 530 S. King St., Downtown, honolulucitylights.org, @friendshonolulucitylights

 

SEE ALSO: Your Insider Guide to Honolulu City Lights

 

Kaimukī Christmas Parade & Tree Lighting

Thursday, Dec. 3, 6 p.m.

The Kaimukī Christmas Parade returns with marching bands, scout troops, schools, businesses, walkers, trollies and Santa, altogether about 40 groups. The Christmas tree on top of Pu‘u O Kaimukī will also be lit.

 

Free, Wai‘alae Ave., Kaimukī, kaimukihawaii.com

 

 

Wahiawā Santa Parade

Friday, Dec. 4, 6:30 to 8:30 p.m.

See Wahiawā light up in its biggest event of the holiday season. The parade will start at Ka‘ala Elementary, go up California Ave. and end at North Cane St. The Wahiawā Community & Business Association is also fundraising to help keep the parade tradition alive—donate online.

 

Free, California Ave., Wahiawā, ourwahiawa.com, @ourwahiawa

 

 

Mililani Holiday Parade

Saturday, Dec. 5, 9 to 10:30 a.m.

The parade featuring marching bands, antique cars, Santa Claus and more starts at Mililani High School’s Kauinana Stadium and ends at the Town Center of Mililani.

 

Free, Mililani, mililanishoppingcenter.com

 

 

Kāne‘ohe Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 5, 9 a.m. to noon

The parade starts at Windward Mall and ends at Castle High School, rain or shine.

 

Free, Kāne‘ohe, kaneohechristmasparade.org, @kaneohechristmasparade

 

 

Wai‘anae Coast Rotary Community Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 5, 5:30 to 9:30 p.m.

Sponsored by Wai‘anae Coast Rotary Club, this parade will start at Wai‘anae Mall and end at Wai‘anae High School.

 

Free, Wai‘anae

 

 

Mānoa Community Christmas Parade

Sunday, Dec. 6, 4 to 6 p.m.

Sponsored by the East Mānoa Lions Club, this parade will start at Noelani School and end at Mānoa Valley District Park.

 

Free, Mānoa, malamamanoa.org

 

 

Pearl City Christmas Parade

Sunday, Dec. 6, 4 to 6 p.m.

Sponsored by Pearl City Shopping Center, this parade will start at Momilani Elementary School and end at Pearl City Shopping Center.

 

Free, Pearl City, mypearlcity.com

 

 

Kapahulu-Mō‘ili‘ili Christmas Parade

Thursday, Dec. 10, 6:30 to 7:30 p.m.

Sponsored by the Kapahulu-Mō‘ili‘ili Lions Club, this parade will start at Kūhiō Elementary School and end at Isenberg St. in front of Old Stadium Park.

 

Free, Kapahulu and Mō‘ili‘ili

 

 

Hale‘iwa Town Christmas Parade

Friday, Dec. 11, 5:30 to 9 p.m.

Sponsored by the North Shore Chamber of Commerce, this parade will start at Weed Circle and end at Hale‘iwa Beach Park.

 

Free, Hale‘iwa

 

 

‘Aiea Community Association Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 12, 8 to 10:30 a.m.

Sponsored by the ‘Aiea Community Association, this parade will start at the Pearlridge Elementary School parking lot and end at ‘Aiea Public Library.

 

Free, ‘Aiea

 

 

‘Ewa Beach Lions Club Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 12, 8 to 11:30 a.m.

Sponsored by the ‘Ewa Beach Lions Club, this parade will start and end at Campbell High School parking lot.

 

Free, ‘Ewa Beach

 

 

Waimānalo Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 12, 9 to 11:30 a.m.

Sponsored by Hawai‘i Pa‘u Riders, this parade will start at Kumuhau St. and Humunuiki St. and end at Waimānalo Beach Park.

 

Free, Waimānalo

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Hawai‘i Kai Marina Community Association

 

Festival of Lights Christmas Boat Parade

Saturday, Dec. 19, sunset

Come see the marina boats decked out and lit up in a parade on the water, and vote for your favorites.

 

Free, Hawai‘i Kai Marina, Hawai‘i Kai, hawaiikaimarina.com, @hkmca_hawaii

 

 

Moanalua Christmas Parade

Saturday, Dec. 19, 6:30 to 8 p.m.

Sponsored by Called Ministry Inc., this parade will start at and end at Moanalua High School parking lot.

 

Free, Moanalua

 

 

Olomana Christmas Parade

Sunday, Dec. 20, 2 to 3 p.m.

Sponsored by the Olomana Community Association, this parade will start at and end at Maunawili Elementary School.

 

Free, Olomana

 

 

Shopping

 

SEE ALSO: Can’t-Miss Local Holiday Markets and Craft Fairs on O‘ahu

 

Habilitat’s Christmas Tree Project

Open daily starting Friday, Nov. 20, noon to 9 p.m.

Shop wreaths, door charms and noble, grand and Douglas firs for your holiday décor. Proceeds go toward the nonprofit that’s been working to help people overcome substance abuse and other antisocial behaviors for more than 40 years. This year’s retail locations are at Central Union Church, Stadium Mall, Hawai‘i Kai Safeway and Kāne‘ohe Bay Shopping Center.

 

Tree prices from $82, habilitat.com

 

 

Shop Small Kailua Gift with Purchase

Nov. 21–29

Shop at participating Kailua stores and spend a combined total of $150 or more to receive a free, limited-edition Oceans End x Kailua Town luggage tag. See the rules here.

 

Kailua Town, kailuatownhi.com, @kailuatownhi

 

 

Christmas Tree Sale at Helemano Farms

Saturday, Nov. 21, and Sunday, Nov. 22, 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. (only Norfolk pines and cypress available)

Friday, Nov. 27, to Sunday, Nov. 29, 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.

Wednesday, Dec. 2, to Wednesday, Dec. 23

  • Monday and Tuesday: closed
  • Wednesday, Thursday and Friday: noon to 6:30 p.m.
  • Saturday and Sunday: 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.

Head to this family farm in Wahiawā to pick your own Norfolk pine or cypress tree grown right here in Hawai‘i. The whole ‘ohana (even dogs!) can search the farm for the perfect tree.

 

$70–$290 for Norfolk pine (up to 12 feet), $80–$340 for a cypress (up to 12 feet), 1750 Whitmore Ave., Wahiawā, helemanofarms.com

 

 

Christmas Tree Sales by Richard Tajiri’s Christmas Hawai‘i

Open daily from Nov. 21, 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Thanksgiving, Nov. 27: 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.

Richard Tajiri’s Christmas Hawai‘i will be selling Noble firs, Nordman firs, Fraser firs, Douglas firs and Grand firs.

 

Behind the Varsity Building, 1212 University Ave., Mānoa, christmastreesinhawaii.com

 

 

Holiday Gift with Purchase at Royal Hawaiian Center

Nov. 25 to Dec. 3

Spend $500 or more to receive a complimentary water bottle carrying bag in one of three colorways. On top of that, spend $5,000 to receive a curated box of premium items from Center merchants. Redeem your receipts at Helumoa Hale Guest Services in Building B, Level 1.

 

Royal Hawaiian Center, 2201 Kalākaua Ave., Waikīkī, royalhawaiiancenter.com, @royalhwnctr

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Kāhala Mall

 

Gift with Purchase at Kāhala Mall

Friday, Nov. 27, to Sunday, Dec. 6

While shopping Black Friday and holiday deals, spend $400 or more to receive a free, limited-edition Aloha Collection x Kāhala Mall insulated cooler bag, while supplies last. Redeem your receipts at Center Court Nov. 27–29 and Dec. 5–6. Rules and restrictions apply.

 

Kāhala Mall, 4211 Wai‘alae Ave., Kāhala, kahalamallcenter.com, @kahalamall

 

 

12 Days of Christmas in Kailua

Dec. 1–13

Pick up a holiday passport and get it stamped at participating merchants. You can redeem the completed passport for a free, limited-edition 12-pack of Hawai‘i-inspired holiday postcards while supplies last.

 

Kailua Town, kailuatownhi.com, @kailuatownhi

 

 

25% Off Holiday Savings Pass at Kāhala Mall

Dec. 4–6

Pick up a printed pass at Carousel Candyland (while supplies last) or print one from the Kāhala Mall website to get 25% off one regular-priced item at 20 participating merchants.

 

Free, Kāhala Mall, 4211 Wai‘alae Ave., Kāhala, kahalamallcenter.com, @kahalamall

 

 

Sip, Shop & Sparkle!

Saturday, Dec. 5, 5:30 to 9 p.m.

Sip unlimited wines and mocktails and enjoy holiday bites while shopping exclusive offers at participating merchants.

 

 

$45 pre-sale, $55 at the door, Ka Makana Ali‘i, 91-5431 Kapolei Parkway, Kapolei, kamakanaalii.com, @kamakanaalii, @honolulumag

 

SEE ALSO: Sip, Shop & Sparkle Presented by Ka Makana Ali‘i

 

Very Merry Event at Kāhala Mall

Dec. 11–13

Buy Very Merry Event ticket pamphlets to support your favorite nonprofits. The pamphlet is full of offers from 45+ participating Kāhala Mall merchants. You can also enter to win a one-night staycation at the Kāhala Hotel & Resort with a breakfast for two at The Plumeria Beach House and $100 Kāhala Mall merchant gift cards.

 

$5 for a ticket pamphlet, Kāhala Mall, 4211 Wai‘alae Ave., Kāhala, kahalamallcenter.com, @kahalamall

 

 

Gift With Purchase at Kāhala Mall

Dec. 11–20

Spend a combined minimum subtotal of $300 to receive a free exclusive Kāhala Mall mini travel case and matching Kāhala Mall luggage strap. Redeem your receipts at Center Court Dec. 11 and Dec. 12 from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. and Dec. 13 to Dec. 20 from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., while supplies last. Rules and restrictions apply.

 

Kāhala Mall, 4211 Wai‘alae Ave., Kāhala, kahalamallcenter.com, @kahalamall

 

 

Food & Drinks

 

Photos: Andrea Lee

 

Good Eats & Pop-Up Treats at Kapa Hale

Wednesday, Nov. 25

11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. noodle bar, bake sale, pop-up shops

5 to 6 p.m. happy hour noodle bar

Kapa Hale brings back its annual pre-Thanksgiving noodle bar and baked good sale with pop-up appearances by other small businesses. The offerings range from smoked turkey pho and duck ramen to pumpkin butter mochi and the Kāhala Shuffle Mud Pie. See the full list of dishes and baked goods available online. Plus, shop the pop-ups Mango House Floral, Slice by HB Baking and Kahalu‘u Kitchen by Shinsato Farm. Preview the food in this reel.

 

Call (808) 888-2060 to pre-order baked goods or go online, Kapa Hale, 4614 Kīlauea Ave., Suite 102, Kāhala, kapahale.com, @4614kapahale

 

SEE ALSO: Christmas and New Year’s Special Menus at O‘ahu Restaurants

 

Holiday Pop-Up Bar at Prince Waikīkī

Nov. 27 and 28, Dec. 4, 5, 11, 12, 18 and 19, 3 to 7 p.m.

Have a festive cocktail or drink in the Prince Waikīkī lobby.

 

Prince Waikīkī, 100 Holomoana St., Waikīkī, princewaikiki.com, @princewaikiki

 

SEE ALSO: Holiday Crafts and Recipes to Try with Your Family This Year

 

Entertainment & Special Holiday Events

 

Letters to Santa at Ala Moana Center

Nov. 2–Dec. 24

Find the Letters to Santa mailbox near the children’s play area on Level 3 Mauka Wing. There will be free stationery available for letter writing.

 

Free, Ala Moana Center Level 3 Mauka Wing, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd., Ala Moana, alamoanacenter.com, @alamoanacenter

 

 

The Night Between

Nov. 21 and 27–29, Dec. 4–6, 11–13 and 18–20

Thursday through Sunday, 6 to 9 p.m.

Join an immersive holiday adventure to take on challenges and help save Christmas.

 

$28 adults, $25 keiki (ages 3–11), keiki under 3 free, former Hub Coworking space, 1050 Queen St., Suite 100, Kaka‘ako, thenightbetween.com, @thenightbetween

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Ward Village

 

Elf Scavenger Hunt in Ward Village

Nov. 27 to Dec. 15

The elves return to Ward Village this holiday season—find them for a chance to win a $100 gift card to the store or restaurant of your choice. Take photos of the elves and post them to your social media account to enter. More details and rules online.

 

Free, Ward Village, 1240 Ala Moana Blvd., Kaka‘ako, wardvillage.com, @wardvillage

 

 

Ala Moana Hula Shows

Nov. 27 to Dec. 24, daily 3 p.m.

Keiki Hula Shows: Sundays at 3 p.m.

The holiday-themed hula show series kicks off on Black Friday, presenting traditional Hawaiian and classic holiday songs at Centerstage. Plus, check out the keiki hula dancers on Sundays.

 

Free, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd., Ala Moana, alamoanacenter.com, @alamoanacenter

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Kāhala Mall

 

Holiday Performances at Kāhala Mall Center Stage

Nov. 27 to Dec. 20

Various studios, ensembles, bands and hālau hula will take Center Stage to share holiday joy through song and dance.

 

Free, 4211 Wai‘alae Ave., Kāhala, kahalamallcenter.com, @kahalamall

 

 

Winter-Themed Keiki Crafts

Friday, Nov. 27, 2 to 4 p.m.

Bring your keiki to make holiday crafts and receive free treats from Zippy’s.

 

Free, Town Center of Mililani center court, 95-1249 Meheula Parkway, Mililani, towncenterofmililani.com, @towncenterofmililani

 

 

Christmas Wreath-Making at KraftStories

Starting on Nov. 27, every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 6 p.m.

Make a full-size Christmas wreath on a grapevine base with the guidance of your instructor. All supplies are provided, and you can BYOB.

 

$89, kama‘āina save 10%, 15 N Pauahi St., Chinatown, kraftstories.com, @kraftstoriesofficial

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Prince Waikīkī

 

Ballet Hawai‘i Holiday Performance

Nov. 28, 6 p.m.

Dec. 5, 5 p.m.

Dec. 20, 6 p.m.

See Ballet Hawai‘i put on a special mini performance of The Nutcracker in the Prince Waikīkī lobby.

 

Free, Prince Waikīkī, 100 Holomoana St., Waikīkī, princewaikiki.com, @princewaikiki

 

 

Pajama Party Movies

Nov. 28 and 29, Dec. 5, 6, 12 and 13

Get in the Christmas spirit with holiday films Elf, The Polar Express and Dr. Seuss’ The Grinch. Movie times vary by theater.

 

From $5, Consolidated Theatres Ward, Kāhala, Kapolei and Mililani, consolidatedtheatres.com, @consolidatedhi

 

 

Phamily Fun Day: Santa at the Hangar

Saturday, Nov. 28, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Make holiday crafts, try flying remote-control aircrafts, write letters to Santa and take photos with the big man himself (for additional fee), plus more family-friendly activities await at the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum.

 

$5 for kama‘āina and military (ages 4+) with pre-registration, $10 at the door, free for museum members and keiki 3 and under, Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, 319 Lexington Blvd., Pearl Harbor, pearlharboraviationmuseum.org, @pearlharboraviationmuseum

 

 

Voices of Aloha at Barnes & Noble Bookfairs

Sunday, Nov. 29, 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Bring your keiki to make Christmas crafts from 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. while enjoying live Christmas carols from noon to 5 p.m. Part of the day’s sales at B&N will benefit Voices of Aloha.

 

Free, donations welcome, Barnes & Noble at Ala Moana Center, 1450 Ala Moana Blvd., Suite 1272, Ala Moana, voicesofaloha.com, @voicesofaloha

 

 

Photo: Andrea Lee

 

’Twas the Light Before Christmas on Ice

Dec. 1 to Jan. 3

This unique immersive experience transforms the Convention Center into a Christmas wonderland with enchanting backdrops, whimsical light sculptures, festive scenes and an indoor ice skating rink. Don’t forget to grab a themed drink and check out the gift shop.

 

 

From $30 (discounts available for keiki, kūpuna and military), free for keiki age 2 and younger, Hawai‘i Convention Center, 1801 Kalākaua Ave., Ala Moana, alohaimmersive.com, @twas.honolulu

 

SEE ALSO: Your Insider Guide to ‘Twas the Light Before Christmas

 

Merry Shop & Strolls

Dec. 2, 9, 16 and 23, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

Every Wednesday, Ka Makana Ali‘i will host a themed evening of family fun with character meet-and-greets, activities, hula performances and gifts with purchases.

 

Free, Ka Makana Ali‘i, 91-5431 Kapolei Parkway, Kapolei, kamakanaalii.com, @kamakanaalii, @kamakanaalii

 

 

Christmas Spectacular

Dec. 4–22, every Friday, Saturday, Sunday + Monday, Dec. 21, and Tuesday, Dec. 22

Enjoy a snow and light show, take a pic with Santa, drink hot chocolate, make s’mores and decorate a gingerbread house. Plus, don’t miss the original musical The Year Christmas Was Almost Canceled in the auditorium below the chapel. This event is cashless—use card or mobile payments.

 

Free admission, purchase scrips for activities, ticket price for the musical TBA, Sacred Hearts Academy, 3253 Wai‘alae Ave., Kaimukī, moolelostudios.square.site, @moolelo.studios

 

 

Aloha Friday Holiday Music Series

Dec. 4, 11 and 18, 5 to 7 p.m.

Stop by Victoria Ward Park Mauka on Friday night to catch live holiday music by local artists and sip a free cup of hot cocoa. See the music lineup online.

 

Free, Victoria Ward Park Mauka, 1020 Auahi St., Kaka‘ako, wardvillage.com, @wardvillage

 

 

Candlelight: Christmas Carols on Strings

Friday, Dec. 4, 6:15 and 8:30 p.m.

Friday, Dec. 18, 6:30 and 8:45 p.m.

Enjoy “12 Days of Christmas,” “Deck the Halls”  and more holiday classics in the ambiance of a candlelit room.

 

 

From $46.50, The Cathedral of St. Andrew, 229 Queen Emma Square, Downtown, feverup.com

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Outrigger Waikīkī Beach Resort

 

Santa Arrives on a Canoe

Saturday, Dec. 5, 9 to 11 a.m.

Watch Santa touch down on Waikīkī Beach via outrigger canoe and enjoy keiki hula performances. Head to Duke’s stage afterward to snap a pic with Santa and get balloon and body art for your keiki.

 

Free, Outrigger Waikīkī Beach Resort, 2335 Kalākaua Ave., Waikīkī, event.outrigger.com, @outriggerwaikiki

 

 

Mililani Holiday Parade After-Party

Saturday, Dec. 5, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

The Mililani Holiday Parade ends at Town Center of Mililani, but the fun doesn’t stop there. Stick around for photos with Santa, prizes, holiday crafts for keiki, face painting and glitter tattoos.

 

Free, Town Center of Mililani Center Court, 95-1249 Mehe‘ula Parkway, Mililani, towncenterofmililani.com, @towncenterofmililani

 

 

Holiday Pawtraits at The Public Pet

Saturday, Dec. 5, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Bring your furry family members to take a Christmas family photo to remember, featuring up to four adults and up to two large pets or three small pets. Photographer Crystal will combine photos from your 15-minute session into one magnificent portrait featuring your family seated on your pet’s back.

 

$99 pre-session reservations, $125 walk-ins, The Public Pet, 3422 Wai‘alae Ave., Suite 101, Kaimukī, crystalrphotography.studio, @crystalrphotography, @thepublicpet

 

 

Santa Saturday Keiki Carnival

Saturday, Dec. 5, 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

Head to Kapolei Shopping Center to meet Santa and Rudolph, play keiki carnival games and marvel at a stilt-walker, juggler and other entertainment.

 

Free, Kapolei Shopping Center, 590 Farrington Highway, Kapolei, kapoleishopping.com, @kapoleishoppingctr

 

 

Mele Kalikimaka, Ei Nei

Saturday, Dec. 5, 7 p.m.

Beloved local band Ei Nei puts on a Christmas concert with special guest Izik.

 

 

From $47.50, Hawai‘i Theatre, 1130 Bethel St., Downtown, hawaiitheatre.com, @hawaiitheatre

 

 

Jingle Rock Run

Sunday, Dec. 6, 3 p.m.

The festivities start at 3 p.m., there’s a Keiki Sprint at 4 p.m. for those 12 and younger and the run starts at 5 p.m. This is a fundraiser for Make-A-Wish Hawai‘i.

 

$40 adults (13+), $30 keiki (2–12), keiki under 2 free and no registration required, Kaka‘ako Waterfront Park, 102 Ohe St., Kaka‘ako,  jinglerockrun.com, @makeawishhawaii

 

 

Ho‘okena for the Holidays

Sunday, Dec. 6, 6 p.m.

Hear island-style holiday music from Nā Hōkū Hanohano Award-winning band Ho‘okena with special guest Maila Gibson.

 

 

$35–$45, Blue Note Hawai‘i, 2335 Kalākaua Ave., Waikīkī, bluenotejazz.com, @bluenotehawaii

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Hawaiian Humane Society

 

Deck the Howls

Kosasa Family Campus at Ho‘opili: Sunday, Dec. 6, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., 6 to 7 p.m.

Mō‘ili‘ili Campus: Monday, Dec. 7, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., 6 to 7 p.m.

Bring your keiki to spend quality time reading to shelter animals. They’ll also get to decorate stockings for the animals and take home hot cocoa and cookies. Sign up fast since there are only 15 spaces for each time slot.

 

 

Free, registration required, Hawaiian Humane Society Kosasa Family Campus at Ho‘opili, 91-1945 Fort Weaver Road, ‘Ewa Beach; Hawaiian Humane Society Mō‘ili‘ili Campus, 2700 Wai‘alae Ave., Mō‘ili‘ili; hawaiianhumane.org, @hawaiianhumane

 

 

Beaded Ornament Workshop at Sugarcane

Monday, Dec. 7, 4 p.m.

Your ticket includes all supplies needed to make an adorable beaded holiday ornament plus a holiday cocktail and baked goods.

 

For ages 12+, $40, 1137 11th Ave., #101, Kaimukī, sugarcanekaimuki.com, @sugarcanehawaii

 

 

Mariah Carey Christmas Tribute by Jiayin

Monday, Dec. 7, 7 p.m.

Hear Jiayin and friends pay tribute to Mariah Carey’s greatest holiday hits.

 

 

$20–$25, Blue Note Hawai‘i, 2335 Kalākaua Ave., Waikīkī, bluenotejazz.com, @bluenotehawaii

 

 

Kaia Soul – A Very Soulful Christmas

Tuesday, Dec. 8, 7 p.m.

Trains & Trolleys

 

Photo: Courtesy of Pearlridge Center

 

Pearlridge Express Holiday Train

Nov. 21 through Dec. 18

  • Monday to Friday: noon to 7 p.m. (including Black Friday)
  • Saturday: 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
  • Sunday: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Closed on Thanksgiving, Nov. 26

Dec. 19 through Jan. 3

  • Monday to Saturday: 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
  • Sunday: 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
  • Closes at 6 p.m. on Christmas Eve (Thursday, Dec. 24), New Year’s Eve (Thursday, Dec. 31) and New Year’s Day (Friday, Jan. 1)

Jan. 4 through Jan. 10

  • Monday to Friday: noon to 7 p.m.
  • Saturday: 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.
  • Sunday: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

All keiki aboard! Watch your little ones’ eyes light up as they ride the custom miniature train across Pearlridge Center Mauka’s festive landscape filled with oversized toys. Taking a ride on Hawai‘i’s only scale-model, fully functioning locomotive has become a holiday tradition for many. Plus, train booklets include a free photo with Santa at the Pearlridge Center Santa Set in Wai Makai. On Black Friday, keiki can ride for free from 8 to 10 a.m. (one ride per keiki).

 

$6 per ride, $41 10-ride coupon books, keiki must be under 48 inches tall, 98-1005 Moanalua Road, ‘Aiea, pearlridgeonline.com, @pearlridge

 

 

Photo: Courtesy of Prince Waikīkī

 

Holly Jolly Waikīkī Trolley

Dec. 6–25, daily at 6, 7 and 8 p.m (8:30 p.m. instead of 8 p.m. on Fridays)

Hop on the trolley at Prince Waikīkī and enjoy a round-trip ride to see the holiday decorations at Honolulu City Lights. The last of the Friday night rides is a little later, so you and your ‘ohana can watch the Waikīkī fireworks before getting on the trolley.

 

 

$30 for adults and keiki ages 3 and up, lap children are free, pickup at Prince Waikīkī, 100 Holomoana St., Waikīkī, princewaikiki.com, @princewaikiki

 

 

Holiday Lights Trolley Tour

Sunday, Dec. 6, through Thursday, Dec. 31, tours depart at 6, 7 and 8 p.m.

Take a joyful 30-minute ride to Honolulu Hale to see Shaka Santa, then spend about an hour exploring all the lights and scenes throughout the area. Reservations are required and can fill up quickly. Tickets also include free cocoa, entry into the Holiday Lights & Music Show and a photo with Santa Claus. A $10 shuttle service from Waikīkī to Winter Wonderland is available.

 

 

$39.50–$49.50 for adults; $34.50–$39.50 for keiki 3 to 11 years old; kids 2 years and younger are free but must sit on an adult’s lap, pickup at the corner of Richards St. and Aloha Tower Dr., holidaylightshi.com, @holidaylightshi

Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.

Manage Consent Preferences

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
  • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.

Vendor preferences

Confirm our vendors
